enrichment.short_title: Whether £10,000 property contribution created resulting trust or repayable loan

statutes_considered.title: Limitation Act 1980
provisions: general limitation periods (discussed as inapplicable to resulting trusts)

key_facts: Dr Ravi Vajpeyi claimed a 33.89% resulting trust in 108 Brigstock Road after providing £10,000 of the 1980 purchase price, registered solely in Mr Shuaib Yusaf's name.
She also claimed repayment of a £100,000 loan secured by charge on Brigstock Road arising from the 1994 sale of 2 Warminster Road.
The parties had a long unconventional personal relationship; the defendant proved repayments of £10,000 and £95,929.89, leaving £4,070.11 admitted outstanding.
The defendant contended both sums were loans repaid; the claimant said payments were gifts or unrelated business dealings.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Trial in the Chancery Division following unsuccessful settlement adjournment.
enrichment.outcome: Claim dismissed except for £4,070.11 balance admitted due; counterclaim for redemption succeeded in principle subject to that sum.
enrichment.ratio: The presumption of a resulting trust from provision of purchase money may be weak and rebutted where, on the common-sense view of the circumstances, the contribution was a loan rather than a shared investment; long delay in asserting a beneficial interest and conduct treating the property as the defendant's alone may help rebut the presumption.
legal_issues: Strength of presumption of resulting trust and evidence required to rebut it
Whether £10,000 was loan or capital contribution
Whether loans of £10,000 and £100,000 were repaid
Estoppel by convention
Whether interest was payable on interest-free loan agreement

enrichment.short_title: Article 3 threshold for asylum support after late asylum claim under section 55
key_facts: Three asylum seekers were refused support under section 55 because claims were not made as soon as reasonably practicable after arrival.
Maurice Kay J held section 55(5) required support to avoid Article 3 breaches for all three; the Secretary of State appealed as to applicant T only.
Applicant S's destitution with medical evidence of malnutrition and psychological disturbance clearly engaged Article 3; that finding was not challenged.
Applicant T slept at Heathrow from 18 April 2003 with noise, limited washing facilities and minor health complaints but had shelter and some food money.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Secretary of State's appeal to the Court of Appeal from Administrative Court judgment on section 55(5) and Article 3 ECHR.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed in relation to T; his condition had not reached or verged on inhuman or degrading treatment under Article 3.
enrichment.ratio: There is no simple test for when denial of asylum support becomes inhuman or degrading under Article 3; each case depends on all circumstances, and the claimant must establish necessity to a high standard—homelessness alone does not suffice where basic shelter and means remain.
legal_issues: Interpretation of section 55(5) and interaction with Article 3
Threshold for inhuman or degrading treatment in destitution cases
Burden and standard of proof on asylum seekers
Comparison of severity between different applicants

enrichment.short_title: Whether court should direct CCRC to refer conviction without fresh investigation
key_facts: Mr Boyle sought judicial review of the Criminal Cases Review Commission's refusal to refer his 1997 conviction to the Court of Appeal.
Henriques J had granted permission on strongly arguable grounds; the CCRC agreed to a fresh review with new personnel.
Boyle asked the court to order an immediate reference rather than await further CCRC investigation.
Five disputed issues included bullet-evidence expert reports, alleged perjury by a senior police officer, prosecution conduct, and witness reliability.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Substantive judicial review hearing before Moses J after permission granted by Henriques J.
enrichment.outcome: Mandatory reference refused; CCRC decisions of November 2001 quashed and fresh review ordered with specific investigative directions; no order as to costs; damages claim refused.
enrichment.ratio: Even where grounds for referral appear strong, it is for the CCRC—not the Administrative Court—to investigate facts and decide whether to refer; the court should not substitute its own fact-finding for the statutory review body.
legal_issues: Whether court may direct CCRC to refer a case without fresh investigation
Scope of judicial review of CCRC decisions
Appropriate remedy where CCRC agrees to reconsider

enrichment.short_title: Summary judgment on telecom circuit lease debts after WorldCom bankruptcy
key_facts: WorldCom claimed £1,592,614.62 plus interest for unpaid annual and upgrade charges under capitalised telecom circuit lease agreements with Primus.
Primus terminated all agreements after WorldCom's Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 2002.
Primus sought to amend its defence to rescind for alleged misrepresentations as to WorldCom's financial viability and other technical and contractual defects.
Ms McKibbin of WorldCom UK had told Primus during negotiations that WorldCom was financially sound and would be 'there for the full 10 years'.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Concurrent CPR Part 24 summary judgment application and application for permission to amend defence and counterclaim.
enrichment.outcome: Summary judgment for WorldCom; amended defence and counterclaim held to have no real prospect of success.
enrichment.ratio: An in-house lawyer negotiating contract wording had no actual or apparent authority to make representations about the parent company's future financial viability; section 2(1) Misrepresentation Act 1967 liability looks to the belief of the contracting party, not its agent, and entire agreement clauses limited to 'Capacity' did not exclude such representations.
legal_issues: Authority to make pre-contract representations
Innocent and negligent misrepresentation and rescission after part performance
Construction of entire agreement and warranty exclusion clauses
Void or voidable duplicate agreements and upgrade misrepresentation
Measure of damages under section 2(1)

enrichment.short_title: Appeal against restraining advertisement of rent-based winding-up petition
key_facts: Landlord James Dolman & Company Ltd presented a winding-up petition based on £25,000 unpaid rent for August 2002 to July 2003.
The petition was intended to pre-empt county court rent recovery proceedings claiming over £130,000 for earlier periods.
The company asserted set-offs including asbestos contamination and occupation by the landlord, but these were largely unquantified or related to earlier periods.
Norris J found no substantial bona fide dispute yet restrained advertisement pending trial of the separate rent claim.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal with leave from Chancery judge's order restraining advertisement of winding-up petition.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; injunction discharged; petitioner awarded costs below and on appeal.
enrichment.ratio: Where a judge finds no bona fide substantial dispute on the petition debt, restraining advertisement pending unrelated litigation is inconsistent with the practice that winding-up petitions must not be used to decide disputed debts; jurisdiction to restrain exists only to prevent abuse of process.
legal_issues: When advertisement of a winding-up petition may be restrained
Bona fide substantial dispute on petition debt
Set-off and cross-claim against statutory demand debt
Whether petition motivated by parallel proceedings is improper

enrichment.short_title: Permission to appeal on commercial agents compensation after non-renewal
key_facts: Pure Fishing (UK) Ltd manufactured fishing tackle and used fixed six-month agency contracts with commercial agents.
In March 1999 agents refused to sell a new Abu Garcia product range; the principal treated this as breach of good faith and did not renew contracts expiring 30 June 1999.
Agents claimed compensation under regulation 17(6); the principal relied on regulation 18(a) excluding compensation for default justifying immediate termination.
The judge held regulation 17 covered expiry by effluxion of time but regulation 18(a) applied only to express termination by the principal.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Application for permission to appeal from HHJ Kershaw's High Court judgment on commercial agents compensation.
enrichment.outcome: Permission to appeal granted on arguable construction of regulation 18(a) and whether non-renewal after agent default can amount to principal termination.
enrichment.ratio: It is arguable that, where regulation 17 treats expiry by effluxion as termination, regulation 18(a) may likewise treat a principal's failure to renew as termination for default purposes; merits not finally decided at this stage.
legal_issues: Construction of 'termination' in regulations 17 and 18
Whether non-renewal after agent default excludes compensation
Whether agent refusal to market new range justified immediate termination
Relevance of principal's motive in non-renewal

enrichment.short_title: Stay of share-sale proceedings where dispute relates to 1999 agreements
key_facts: Sainsbury bought Edge shares from the Nasharty family under March and October 1999 share sale and shareholders agreements containing ICC Paris arbitration clauses.
In 2001 Amr El Nasharty purportedly signed re-sale and warranty-extension agreements on behalf of all claimants; they denied authority and sued for declarations the 2001 agreements were invalid.
Sainsbury gave warranty notice in March 2003 claiming at least £130 million and commenced ICC arbitration for shareholders agreement breaches.
Claimants brought declaratory proceedings to establish the warranty deadline remained 9 March 2001 if the 2001 extensions were void.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Application to stay Commercial Court proceedings under section 9 Arbitration Act 1996.
enrichment.outcome: Stay granted under section 9; proceedings held 'in relation to' the 1999 share sale agreements including disputes over alleged 2001 variations.
enrichment.ratio: Proceedings seeking declarations that warranty deadlines and deferred consideration rights were not varied are 'in relation to' the underlying 1999 agreements and must be arbitrated under their broad ICC clauses; issue estoppel from court findings would preclude defences otherwise available in arbitration.
legal_issues: Construction of 'in relation to' in arbitration clause
Whether authority dispute is severable from variation dispute
Section 9 stay versus inherent jurisdiction stay
Interaction with existing ICC arbitration

enrichment.short_title: Whether ex-partner may use stored IVF embryos after withdrawal of consent
key_facts: Ms Evans and Mrs Hadley each had frozen embryos created with former partners from whom they had separated and who withdrew consent to storage and use.
Ms Evans had undergone ovarian surgery immediately after egg harvesting; the embryos represented her only chance of a genetically related child.
Clinics could not treat the women without continuing dual consent under Schedule 3 until embryos were transferred.
Claimants sought declarations, injunctions, and optional HRA incompatibility declarations; estoppel and 'use' of embryos arguments were also raised.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Combined trials in the Family Division, first major HFEA consent challenge under the Human Rights Act 1998.
enrichment.outcome: Claims of both Evans and Hadley dismissed; clinics permitted to allow stored embryos to perish.
enrichment.ratio: Schedule 3 requires continuing mutual consent until embryos are 'used' by transfer into the woman; either gamete provider may lawfully withdraw consent beforehand, and this consensual regime is a proportionate Article 8 interference that does not breach Articles 2, 12 or 14; promissory estoppel cannot override the statutory withdrawal right.
legal_issues: Whether clinics may treat one partner alone after relationship breakdown
Meaning of 'used' in Schedule 3 paragraph 4
HRA challenge to consent withdrawal provisions
Promissory estoppel against statutory consent regime
